_meta.control_type: GROUP B — CATEGORY STRUCTURE. The sharpest test in the plan.
_meta.prediction: Viable or Contested band. CRITICAL FAILURE CRITERION: if defensibility scores >= 4, the dimension is measuring 'is this business good' rather than 'is it defensible', and must be rewritten to demand a specific copy-resistance claim.
_meta.purpose: Hill Street Tai Hwa is unambiguously successful — a Michelin STAR held every year since 2016, the only hawker stall in Singapore with one — yet it has almost none of what the rubric's level descriptions call defensibility: no chain, no distribution, no proprietary system, no accumulated institutional trust, no dataset. It has a recipe and a reputation. If the rubric cannot distinguish 'successful' from 'defensible' this case proves it.
_meta.ground_truth: One MICHELIN Star, 2026 Guide, held every year since 2016. One of 12 establishments listed in every Singapore selection since 2016. The only hawker stall with a star.

form.business_name: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle
form.website: (none — no website; the business operates from a hawker stall)
form.category: Bak chor mee (minced pork noodles) — a single hawker stall at 466 Crawford Lane, #01-12. Cooked to order.
form.positioning_sentence: Singapore's best bak chor mee. The only hawker stall in the country with a Michelin star.
form.differentiator: We hold one MICHELIN Star and have held it every single year since 2016 — the only hawker stall in Singapore to do so. Our mee pok is cooked to order and dressed with a specific vinegar-chilli-soy blend, layered with crispy dried plaice, pork liver and crackling. We have been popular since long before the star, and people queue for it even at off-peak hours.
form.undercut_on: Price. We charge $8-15 a bowl, which is two to three times what other bak chor mee stalls charge. Plenty of stalls sell a bowl for $4-5 and some customers will not pay our price or wait in our queue.
form.their_price_point: S$4-5 for a standard bowl at most other bak chor mee stalls.

_expected_reasoning.market_headroom: The hawker food category is real, large and stable, though flat — not a growth category but not a trap. Expected 3-4.
_expected_reasoning.competitive_room: Extremely fragmented (100+ stalls) but no price power at the category level; the $8-15 price is only viable because of the star. Expected 3.
_expected_reasoning.position_availability: **Should be HIGH — this is the incumbent test.** Tai Hwa genuinely owns 'the Michelin-star hawker' position and nobody else holds it. If position_availability scores 2 here as it did for KOI, the dimension is confirmed broken for incumbents. Expected 4-5 if the dimension works.
_expected_reasoning.defensibility: **THE CRITICAL TEST.** What is actually defensible here? A recipe — copyable, and already copied by alumni who opened their own stalls. A reputation built over decades — real but not purchasable or transferable. A Michelin star — awarded annually and revocable, and not the business's asset to control. NO chain, NO system, NO distribution, NO dataset, NO formula. Level 2 ('competitor must do genuine development work') is arguable; level 1 ('copyable in weeks without development') is closer to truth for the recipe itself, though not for the reputation. Expected 2-3. **If it scores 4-5 the dimension is broken.**
_expected_reasoning.demand_reach: A specific, identifiable, queuing customer base — locals plus food tourists. Expected 4-5.

_what_each_outcome_means.defensibility_2_or_3: DIMENSION VALID. It correctly separates 'successful' from 'defensible'. The star is not a moat.
_what_each_outcome_means.defensibility_4_or_5: DIMENSION BROKEN. It is scoring general quality/reputation, not copy-resistance. Rewrite to require a specific, named, non-transferable asset.
_what_each_outcome_means.position_availability_4_or_5: DIMENSION FIXABLE. It works for incumbents who genuinely own a position; the KOI result was about something else.
_what_each_outcome_means.position_availability_2: DIMENSION CONFIRMED BROKEN for incumbents. Two independent strong incumbents both scoring 2 settles it.
